keywords.def: Relating to the indigenous people who built an empire in central Mexico.
A very large and important city.
A raised road or path built across water, wet ground, or low land.
Related to the period when a country was controlled by a foreign power.
Freedom from control by another country or authority.
A major political or social change, often involving conflict or uprising.
The ability to recover quickly from difficulties or adapt to change.

sentences.en: The biggest city in North America isn’t New York or Los Angeles, it’s Mexico City.
sentences.zh: 北美洲最大的城市既不是纽约，也不是洛杉矶，而是墨西哥城。

sentences.en: Mexico City is also the oldest capital city in the entire Americas and the largest Spanish-speaking city in the world.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥城也是整个美洲最古老的首都，以及全球最大的西班牙语城市。

sentences.en: Today, this enormous metropolis is home to over twenty million people.
sentences.zh: 如今，这座庞大的大都市居住着两千多万人口。

sentences.en: But its story began centuries ago, long before the arrival of the Spanish, when it was an island city built by the Aztecs in the middle of a vast lake.
sentences.zh: 但它的故事始于几个世纪前，早在西班牙人到来之前，这里曾是一座由阿兹特克人在浩瀚湖泊中央建造的岛屿城市。

sentences.en: In this episode of Thinking in English, we’re going to explore the incredible history of Mexico City from its origins as the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlán, to its destruction and rebirth under Spanish rule, and finally, to its rise as a vibrant and dynamic modern city.
sentences.zh: 在本期《Thinking in English》节目中，我们将一起探索墨西哥城的传奇历史：从它最初作为阿兹特克首都特诺奇蒂特兰的起源，到它在西班牙统治下的毁灭与重生，再到它最终崛起为充满活力与动感的现代化都市。

sentences.en: At the same time, we will learn some new and useful English vocabulary and practice our listening comprehension at the same time!
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们还将学习一些实用且有趣的新英语词汇，并练习我们的英语听力理解！

sentences.en: Before Mexico City, there was Tenochtitlán, the magnificent capital of the Aztec Empire.
sentences.zh: 在墨西哥城之前，这里是特诺奇蒂特兰，阿兹特克帝国的辉煌首都。

sentences.en: But who were the Aztecs? And how did they come to build one of the most impressive cities in the ancient world?
sentences.zh: 但阿兹特克人是谁？他们又是如何建立起古代世界中最令人瞩目的城市之一的呢？

sentences.en: The Aztecs were a Mesoamerican civilization.
sentences.zh: 阿兹特克人是一个中美洲文明。

sentences.en: “Mesoamerican Civilization” refers to a group of ancient cultures that developed in the region now known as Mexico and Central America, before the arrival of Europeans.
sentences.zh: “中美洲文明”指的是在欧洲人到来之前，在现今被称为墨西哥和中美洲的地区发展起来的一群古代文化。

sentences.en: These civilizations included the Olmec, the Maya, Zapotec and the Aztec.
sentences.zh: 这些文明包括奥尔梅克文明、玛雅文明、萨波特克文明和阿兹特克文明。

sentences.en: They built cities, temples, and pyramids, and they developed their own writing systems and calendars and farming techniques.
sentences.zh: 他们建造了城市、神庙和金字塔，并发展出了自己的文字系统、历法以及农业技术。

sentences.en: The Aztecs were not originally from the Valley of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 阿兹特克人最初并不是墨西哥谷本地人。

sentences.en: According to their own legends, they came from a distant, possibly mythical homeland called Aztlán.
sentences.zh: 根据他们自己的传说，他们来自一个遥远、甚至可能是神话中的故乡，名叫阿兹特兰。

sentences.en: The word Aztec actually means “the people from Aztlán.”
sentences.zh: “阿兹特克”这个词实际上意为“来自阿兹特兰的人”。

sentences.en: The Aztecs also included a number of different groups of people, including the Mexica, who later gave their name to the city, Mexico City, and the country Mexico.
sentences.zh: 阿兹特克人也包含多个不同的群体，其中包括墨西卡人，他们后来给这座城市（墨西哥城）以及国家（墨西哥）带来了名字。

sentences.en: Around the 14th century, the Aztecs migrated into the Valley of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 大约在14世纪，阿兹特克人迁徙到了墨西哥谷。

sentences.en: This is a high altitude basin surrounded by mountains and lakes.
sentences.zh: 这是一个被群山和湖泊环绕的高海拔盆地。

sentences.en: A high altitude basin is a large, flat area of land that is surrounded by mountains and is located high above the sea level.
sentences.zh: 高海拔盆地是指一块周围环绕着山脉、且位于海平面较高位置的大片平坦土地。

sentences.en: According to Aztec legend, their gods told them to build a city where they see an eagle eating a snake while standing on a cactus.
sentences.zh: 根据阿兹特克传说，他们的神明告诉他们，要在他们看到一只老鹰站在仙人掌上吃蛇的地方建立城市。

sentences.en: When the Aztecs saw this vision on a small island in the middle of Lake Texcoco, they had found the place to build a city.
sentences.zh: 当阿兹特克人在特斯科科湖中央的一个小岛上看到这个异象时，他们便找到了建立城市的地方。

sentences.en: And that image of an eagle and a snake is now in the middle of Mexico’s national flag.
sentences.zh: 而那只老鹰和蛇的图案如今就印在墨西哥国旗的正中央。

sentences.en: The Aztecs called their new city Tenochtitlán, and it was founded in 1325.
sentences.zh: 阿兹特克人将他们的新城市命名为特诺奇蒂特兰，它建于1325年。

sentences.en: And I have to apologize if I am pronouncing any of these Aztec words incorrectly.
sentences.zh: 如果我有任何这些阿兹特克语的发音不准确，我得先道个歉。

sentences.en: I’m not the best with my pronunciation of other languages.
sentences.zh: 我对其他语言的发音并不是很在行。

sentences.en: The Aztecs transformed the island in the center of the lake.
sentences.zh: 阿兹特克人改造了湖泊中心的这座岛屿。

sentences.en: It was connected to the mainland by long causeways.
sentences.zh: 它通过长长的堤道与大陆相连。

sentences.en: Causeways are raised roads or paths built across water, wet ground, or low land.
sentences.zh: 堤道是指建在水面、湿地或低洼地带上的高架道路或小径。

sentences.en: The Aztecs built canals for transportation.
sentences.zh: 阿兹特克人修建了用于交通的运河。

sentences.en: And they filled the city with impressive temples, palaces, and marketplaces.
sentences.zh: 他们用令人惊叹的神庙、宫殿和集市填满了这座城市。

sentences.en: They even created floating gardens, which allowed them to grow crops on the surface of the lake.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至创造了浮动花园，这让他们能够在湖面上种植农作物。

sentences.en: At its height, Tenochtitlán may have had a population of more than 200,000 people.
sentences.zh: 在其鼎盛时期，特诺奇蒂特兰的人口可能超过了20万。

sentences.en: This would make it one of the largest and most advanced cities in the entire world, at that time.
sentences.zh: 这使得它在当时成为整个世界中最大、最先进的城市之一。

sentences.en: Life there revolved around religion, trade, and agriculture.
sentences.zh: 那里的生活围绕着宗教、贸易和农业展开。

sentences.en: They also had a complex social hierarchy that organized society into nobles, warriors, priests, and farmers.
sentences.zh: 他们还拥有复杂的社会等级制度，将社会组织为贵族、武士、祭司和农民。

sentences.en: When I said the city was one of the most advanced in the world, I meant it.
sentences.zh: 当我刚说这座城市是世界上最先进的城市之一时，我是认真的。

sentences.en: The Aztecs built things that were not common really anywhere else in the world at that time.
sentences.zh: 阿兹特克人建造的东西在当时的世界上几乎别处罕见。

sentences.en: They had drinkable water brought into the city by aqueducts.
sentences.zh: 他们通过引水渠将饮用水引入城市。

sentences.en: They had a really advanced drainage system, and they had paved streets that were wide and open, almost like you get in modern cities today.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有非常先进的排水系统，并且拥有宽敞开阔的铺装街道，几乎就像你们今天在现代城市中看到的那样。

sentences.en: Tenochtitlán was also the center of the Aztec Empire.
sentences.zh: 特诺奇蒂特兰也是阿兹特克帝国的中心。

sentences.en: Just before the Spanish arrived in the Americas, the Aztec empire stretched from the Pacific Ocean to the Gulf of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 就在西班牙人到达美洲之前，阿兹特克帝国从太平洋一直延伸到墨西哥湾。

sentences.en: Tenochtitlán was a great city, at the heart of an empire, and built on an island in the middle of a lake.
sentences.zh: 特诺奇蒂特兰是一座伟大的城市，处于帝国的核心，并建在湖泊中央的岛屿上。

sentences.en: It was really impressive. By the early 1500s, Tenochtitlán and the Aztec Empire were at the heights of their power.
sentences.zh: 它确实令人叹为观止。到16世纪初，特诺奇蒂特兰和阿兹特克帝国正处于其权力的巅峰。

sentences.en: But across the ocean, another empire had begun to explore and conquer new lands.
sentences.zh: 但在海洋的另一端，另一个帝国已经开始探索并征服新的土地。

sentences.en: Spain. In 1519, a Spanish conquistador named Hernán Cortés arrived on the coast of modern day Mexico.
sentences.zh: 西班牙。1519年，一位名叫埃尔南·科尔特斯的西班牙征服者抵达了现今墨西哥的海岸。

sentences.en: At that time, the Aztec Empire ruled over many smaller peoples in Central Mexico.
sentences.zh: 当时，阿兹特克帝国统治着中美洲的许多小部族。

sentences.en: These groups often resented the more powerful Aztecs because they were forced to pay heavy tributes, like taxes, and sometimes even provide people for human sacrifices.
sentences.zh: 这些群体通常对更加强大的阿兹特克人满怀怨恨，因为他们被迫缴纳沉重的贡赋（比如赋税），有时甚至还要提供活人用于祭祀。

sentences.en: Cortés used this to his advantage. As he marched towards the capital, he made alliances with the enemies of the Aztecs.
sentences.zh: 科尔特斯利用了这一点来为自己谋利。当他向首都进军时，他与阿兹特克人的敌人结成了同盟。

sentences.en: The Aztec Emperor at the time, Moctezuma II, had heard rumors of strange men arriving on the coast.
sentences.zh: 当时的阿兹特克皇帝蒙特苏马二世听说了海岸上有陌生人到达的传言。

sentences.en: According to some accounts, he believed the Spanish might be connected to a returning God from Aztec mythology.
sentences.zh: 根据某些记载，他认为西班牙人可能与阿兹特克神话中归神有关。

sentences.en: Because of this, he chose to welcome Cortés and Cortés’ men when they entered his city.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，当科尔特斯及其手下进入他的城市时，他选择欢迎他们。

sentences.en: When the Spanish reached Tenochtitlán, they were amazed.
sentences.zh: 当西班牙人到达特诺奇蒂特兰时，他们惊呆了。

sentences.en: The city was larger and more beautiful than anything they had seen in Europe.
sentences.zh: 这座城市比他们在欧洲见过的任何东西都要宏大、美丽。

sentences.en: It was full of clean streets and canals and marketplaces.
sentences.zh: 到处都是整洁的街道、运河和集市。

sentences.en: But the Spanish were also shocked by Aztec religious practices, especially human sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 但西班牙人也对阿兹特克的宗教习俗感到震惊，尤其是活人祭祀。

sentences.en: And the Spanish were really just hoping to find some gold.
sentences.zh: 而且西班牙人其实只是希望能找到一些黄金。

sentences.en: Moctezuma was taken hostage and violence broke out in the city.
sentences.zh: 蒙特苏马被劫为人质，城内随即爆发了暴力冲突。

sentences.en: The Aztecs rebelled, forcing the Spanish and their allies to flee.
sentences.zh: 阿兹特克人发动起义，迫使西班牙人及其盟友仓皇逃离。

sentences.en: But Cortez did not give up. He regrouped, gathered more indigenous allies and returned to Tenochtitlán in 1521.
sentences.zh: 但科尔特斯并没有放弃。他重新整顿队伍，集结了更多土著盟友，并于1521年回到了特诺奇蒂特兰。

sentences.en: The Spanish cut off supplies of food and water to the city.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人切断了该市的食物和水供应。

sentences.en: Diseases, especially smallpox, which was brought from Europe, spread through the city, killing thousands.
sentences.zh: 疾病（尤其是从欧洲带过去的天花）在城中蔓延，夺去了成千上万人的生命。

sentences.en: Eventually the Aztec defenses collapsed.
sentences.zh: 最终，阿兹特克的防御崩溃了。

sentences.en: The once great city of Tenochtitlán was destroyed.
sentences.zh: 曾经伟大的特诺奇蒂特兰城被毁。

sentences.en: Its temples were burned and its canals were filled in.
sentences.zh: 它的神庙被焚烧，它的运河被填平。

sentences.en: After the fall of Tenochtitlán, Hernán Cortés began rebuilding the city as the capital of a new Spanish colony called New Spain.
sentences.zh: 在特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，埃尔南·科尔特斯开始将这座城市重建为一个名为“新西班牙”的新西班牙殖民地的首都。

sentences.en: He called his new city, La Ciudad de México or Mexico City.
sentences.zh: 他将他的新城市命名为“墨西哥城”。

sentences.en: The Spanish literally built on top of the Aztecs.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人字面意义上是在阿兹特克人的废墟上建立起这座城市的。

sentences.en: Stones from Aztec temples were used to construct churches and palaces and government buildings.
sentences.zh: 阿兹特克神庙的石头被用来建造教堂、宫殿和政府大楼。

sentences.en: The Great Temple at the center of Tenochtitlán was replaced by the Metropolitan Cathedral.
sentences.zh: 位于特诺奇蒂特兰中心的大神庙被大都会大教堂所取代。

sentences.en: In fact, the Metropolitan Cathedral is still there.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大都会大教堂至今仍然矗立在那里。

sentences.en: It still stands in the center of Mexico City, in its main square.
sentences.zh: 它依然屹立在墨西哥城市中心的宪法广场上。

sentences.en: From Mexico City, Spanish officials ruled a large colony that stretched from California in the north to Central America in the south.
sentences.zh: 从墨西哥城出发，西班牙官员统治着一个庞大的殖民地，北起加利福尼亚，南至中美洲。

sentences.en: And lots of wealth came into the city. There was silver from Mexican mines.
sentences.zh: 大量的财富涌入这座城市。有来自墨西哥矿山的白银。

sentences.en: Goods from Asia, brought by ships across the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 有通过太平洋船只运来的来自亚洲的商品。

sentences.en: And European products imported from Spain.
sentences.zh: 还有从西班牙进口的欧洲产品。

sentences.en: But this wealth was not shared equally. Spanish born elites controlled most of the power and money.
sentences.zh: 但这些财富并没有被平均分配。土生白人精英把持着大部分权力和金钱。

sentences.en: People of mixed heritage, usually Spanish and indigenous mixed, formed a growing middle class.
sentences.zh: 拥有混血血统的人（通常是西班牙血统和土著血统的混血）构成了一个不断壮大的中产阶级。

sentences.en: While indigenous people and enslaved Africans usually lived in poverty and faced harsh discrimination.
sentences.zh: 而土著人民和被奴役的非洲人通常生活在贫困之中，并面临着严重的歧视。

sentences.en: Despite these inequalities, the city did become a place of learning and culture.
sentences.zh: 尽管存在这些不平等，这座城市确实成了一个学习和文化的中心。

sentences.en: The University of Mexico was one of the first universities in the entire Americas, and the city was now filled with monasteries and colonial mansions.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥大学是整个美洲最早的大学之一，如今这座城市到处都是修道院和殖民时期的宅邸。

sentences.en: Mexico city, however, did face frequent floods.
sentences.zh: 然而，墨西哥城确实面临着频繁的洪水。

sentences.en: If you remember, the Aztecs had built their city on top of a lake.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得的话，阿兹特克人是将他们的城市建立在湖泊之上的。

sentences.en: And they had constructed a unique drainage system that worked amazingly well for hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 他们构建了一个独特的排水系统，在几百年里运作得好得出奇。

sentences.en: The Spanish had destroyed the Aztec drainage system and filled in the Aztec canals.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人摧毁了阿兹特克的排水系统，并填平了阿兹特克的运河。

sentences.en: This meant that the city would flood a lot more often.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这座城市发水的频率高得多了。

sentences.en: Earthquakes were another danger. And also diseases regularly spread through the crowded population.
sentences.zh: 地震是另一个危险。此外，疾病也经常在拥挤的人群中蔓延。

sentences.en: Still, Mexico City remained a symbol of Spanish power in the New World, and for 300 years it was the center of Spanish colonial life in the Americas.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，墨西哥城仍然是新世界中西班牙权力的象征，在长达300年的时间里，它是美洲西班牙殖民生活的中心。

sentences.en: But by the early 19th century, the idea of independence began to spread.
sentences.zh: 但到了19世纪初，独立的思想开始传播。

sentences.en: Inspired by the Enlightenment and by revolutions in America and France, people in Mexico began demanding change.
sentences.zh: 受启蒙运动以及美国和法国革命的启发，墨西哥的人们开始要求改变。

sentences.en: In 1810, a Catholic priest named Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla gave a famous speech known as “the Cry of Dolores “, calling for independence from Spain.
sentences.zh: 1810年，一位名叫米格尔·伊达尔戈·伊·科斯蒂利亚的天主教神父发表了一场著名的演讲，被称为“多洛雷斯呼声”，呼吁脱离西班牙独立。

sentences.en: His speech sparked a long and bloody war that lasted over a decade.
sentences.zh: 他的演讲点燃了一场漫长而血腥的战争，持续了十多年之久。

sentences.en: Finally, in 1821, Mexico achieved independence, and Mexico City became the capital of the new Mexican nation.
sentences.zh: 最终，在1821年，墨西哥赢得了独立，墨西哥城成为了新墨西哥国家的首都。

sentences.en: Independence did not bring peace or stability.
sentences.zh: 独立并没有带来和平或稳定。

sentences.en: The young country faced economic problems, political chaos, and foreign invasions.
sentences.zh: 这个年轻的国家面临着经济问题、政治混乱和外国入侵。

sentences.en: Leaders came and went. Power often changed hands through violence rather than elections.
sentences.zh: 领导人走马灯似地换。权力往往通过暴力而非选举易手。

sentences.en: In the mid 1800s, a series of reform movements tried to modernize Mexico.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪中期，一系列改革运动试图使墨西哥实现现代化。

sentences.en: These reforms aim to reduce the power of the Catholic Church, and create some fairer laws and try to modernize education and the economy.
sentences.zh: 这些改革旨在削弱天主教教会的权力，制定更公平的法律，并试图使教育和经济现代化。

sentences.en: Then in the 1860s, Mexico was invaded by France.
sentences.zh: 然后在19世纪60年代，墨西哥遭到法国入侵。

sentences.en: The French installed their own emperor Maximilian of Habsburg, who ruled Mexico for just a few short years.
sentences.zh: 法国人扶植了他们自己的皇帝哈布斯堡王朝的马克西米连，他统治墨西哥仅短短几年时间。

sentences.en: His empire collapsed in 1867 and Maximilian was executed.
sentences.zh: 他的帝国在1867年崩溃，马克西米连被处决。

sentences.en: By the late 19th century under the rule of Porfirio Díaz, Mexico entered a period of modernization and growth.
sentences.zh: 到了19世纪末，在波菲里奥·迪亚斯的统治下，墨西哥进入了一个现代化和增长的时期。

sentences.en: Railways and factories, European style buildings transformed Mexico City.
sentences.zh: 铁路、工厂以及欧洲风格的建筑彻底改变了墨西哥城。

sentences.en: The streets were redesigned, public parks were built, and electricity and street cars appeared.
sentences.zh: 街道被重新规划，公共公园建成，电力和有轨电车也出现了。

sentences.en: From the outside, the capital looked modern and prosperous, but inequality and poverty grew worse.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，首都显得现代而繁荣，但财富不均和贫困却在恶化。

sentences.en: The wealth and the progress was mainly concentrated in the hands of a small elite, while most Mexicans remained poor and powerless.
sentences.zh: 财富和进步主要集中在少数精英手中，而大多数墨西哥人依然贫困且毫无权力。

sentences.en: In 1910, the Mexican revolution began. It was one of the most important social revolutions of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 1910年，墨西哥革命爆发。这是20世纪最重要的社会革命之一。

sentences.en: The revolution was a complex conflict involving peasants, workers, rebels, and intellectuals, all demanding change.
sentences.zh: 这场革命是一场复杂的冲突，涉及农民、工人、叛军和知识分子，所有人都要求变革。

sentences.en: Famous revolutionary leaders like Pancho Villa in the North fought to give land and rights back to the ordinary people.
sentences.zh: 像北方的潘乔·维拉这样的著名革命领袖为将土地和权利归还给普通人民而战。

sentences.en: The fighting lasted for a decade, destroying much of the country, but it also changed Mexico’s future.
sentences.zh: 战火持续了十年，摧毁了国家的大部分地区，但也改变了墨西哥的未来。

sentences.en: After the revolution, Mexico City remained the capital of a slightly more democratic and nationalistic Mexico.
sentences.zh: 革命结束后，墨西哥城依然是一个更加民主和民族主义色彩的墨西哥的首都。

sentences.en: The government promoted education and workers’ rights.
sentences.zh: 政府大力推进教育和劳工权利。

sentences.en: Then in the 1920s and 1930s, Mexico City had somewhat of a Golden Age, especially in terms of art and culture.
sentences.zh: 然后在20世纪20和30年代，墨西哥城迎来了一个某种意义上的黄金时代，特别是在艺术和文化方面。

sentences.en: You may have heard of painters like Diego Rivera and Frida Kahlo.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过像迭戈·里维拉和弗里达·卡洛这样的画家。

sentences.en: Rivera’s huge murals on public buildings told the story of Mexico’s indigenous roots, colonial past, and revolutionary struggles.
sentences.zh: 里维拉在公共建筑上的巨幅壁画讲述了墨西哥的土著根基、殖民过去以及革命斗争的故事。

sentences.en: In 1968, Mexico City hosted the Olympic Games.
sentences.zh: 1968年，墨西哥城主办了奥运会。

sentences.en: This was a sign that Mexico City was considered a modern and successful city.
sentences.zh: 这标志着墨西哥城被视为一座现代且成功的城市。

sentences.en: But that same year, political tensions erupted in the tragic Tlatelolco massacre, when government forces killed student protestors.
sentences.zh: 但在同一年，政治紧张局势在悲惨的特拉特洛尔科大屠杀中爆发，当时政府军队杀害了学生抗议者。

sentences.en: As the 20th century continued, Mexico City expanded rapidly.
sentences.zh: 随着20世纪的延续，墨西哥城急剧扩张。

sentences.en: People from across the country moved to the capital looking for jobs and better lives.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的人们为了寻找工作和更好的生活而涌向首都。

sentences.en: The city’s population exploded from around 1 million people in the 1940s to more than 10 million by the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 城市人口从1940年代的大约100万人激增到1980年代的1000多万人。

sentences.en: Today, Mexico City is one of the largest urban areas in the world, home to over 20 million people in its metropolitan region.
sentences.zh: 如今，墨西哥城是世界上最大的城市区域之一，其大都市圈内居住着超过两千万人口。

sentences.en: Aztec ruins lie beneath skyscrapers. Colonial churches stand beside contemporary museums.
sentences.zh: 阿兹特克人的废墟静静躺在摩天大楼下方。殖民时期的教堂与当代博物馆比邻而立。

sentences.en: And traditional markets operate alongside luxury shopping centers.
sentences.zh: 传统的集市与奢华的购物中心并存运作。

sentences.en: The city faces many challenges. Traffic congestion and air pollution are constant problems.
sentences.zh: 这座城市面临着诸多挑战。交通拥堵和空气污染是常有的难题。

sentences.en: Its location in a former lake makes it vulnerable to earthquakes and flooding.
sentences.zh: 它位于昔日湖泊之上的地理位置，使其极易受到地震和洪水的侵袭。

sentences.en: And social inequality remains visible with wealth concentrated in some areas, while other neighborhoods struggle with poverty.
sentences.zh: 社会不平等现象依然清晰可见，财富集中在某些地区，而其他街区则在贫困中挣扎。

sentences.en: But the city is also a center for music, art, and food.
sentences.zh: 但这座城市同时也是音乐、艺术和美食的中心。

sentences.en: Mexico’s cuisine, Mexico’s City’s cuisine, is seen as one of the best in the entire world.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥的美食——墨西哥城的美食，被视为全世界最棒的美食之一。

sentences.en: And the city attracts millions of visitors every year.
sentences.zh: 这座城市每年吸引着数以百万计的游客。

sentences.en: There are festivals, murals, markets, that all celebrate Mexico’s heritage, while technology and businesses and innovation are pushing the city towards the future.
sentences.zh: 这里有庆祝墨西哥遗产的各种节日、壁画和集市，而科技、商业和创新则推动着这座城市大步迈向未来。

sentences.en: From a small settlement to the Aztec capital to the capital of New Spain and now the capital of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 从一个小定居点到阿兹特克首都，再到新西班牙的首都，以及如今墨西哥的首都。

sentences.en: It has been destroyed and reshaped numerous times, but the city has adapted through centuries of change.​
sentences.zh: 它曾无数次被摧毁和重塑，但这座城市历经数世纪的沧桑变迁，始终在不断适应。

sentences.en: So here is today’s final thought. I have never visited Mexico City, but it is somewhere I would love to visit.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是今天的最后感想。我从未去过墨西哥城，但那里是我很想去游览的地方。

sentences.en: In fact, I was invited by a friend last year, but it was just too expensive for me to fly over for a few days.
sentences.zh: 事实上，去年一位朋友曾邀请我去，但对我来说，飞过去待几天实在太贵了。

sentences.en: I was inspired to record this episode after listening to a few podcasts on the Aztec Empire, and also noticing the large Mexican audience that listen to my show and have requested this episode numerous times.
sentences.zh: 我录制这期节目的灵感来源于听了几期关于阿兹特克帝国的播客，同时也注意到有大量墨西哥听众在收听我的节目，并且多次请求我制作这期节目。

sentences.en: Mexico City’s story is a story of transformation.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥城的历史是一个关于蜕变的故事。

sentences.en: It is a city built on water. That was conquered, rebuilt, expanded, and modernized.
sentences.zh: 这是一座建立在水上的城市。它曾被征服、重建、扩建并现代化。

sentences.en: It is now capital of a large and economically important part of the Americas.
sentences.zh: 它如今是美洲一个规模庞大且在经济上占有重要地位的地区的首都。

sentences.en: So, I’m curious what you think. What do you think makes a city great?
sentences.zh: 所以，我很好奇你们怎么看。你们觉得是什么让一座城市变得伟大？

sentences.en: Is it its size, its history, or its culture?
sentences.zh: 是它的规模、它的历史，还是它的文化？

sentences.en: Would you like to visit Mexico City? And what city should I discuss next in this series?
sentences.zh: 你想去墨西哥城参观吗？在这个系列中，我接下来应该探讨哪座城市呢？
